_source: Mined 2026-08-21 from the zeldaret/tww decompilation at Z:/memRip/sources/tww (read-only) and measured against the real USA disc data extracted from roms/Legend of Zelda, The - The Wind Waker (USA).iso -> res/Msg/bmgres.arc:archive/zel_00.bmg and res/Msg/bmgresh.arc:bmgresh/zel_01.bmg. Every 'source' string is a real file:line in the decomp (paths relative to Z:/memRip/sources/tww); every count is a real count over the disc's DAT1 strings, not an estimate. 'confidence' is per claim: 'confirmed' means the USA (VERSION_USA / VERSION > VERSION_JPN) code path in the decomp proves it; 'enum_only' means the decomp names the enumerator but leaves the meaning as a '?' comment; 'measured' means it comes from the bytes, not the source; 'unknown' means neither. Field names for the INF1 entry come from the decomp's own JMSMesgEntry_c (include/f_op/f_op_msg_mng.h:22-40). Wind Waker does NOT use a d_msg_flow.cpp - that is Twilight Princess; TWW's flow lives in fopMsgM_msgDataProc_c::getString (f_op_msg_mng.cpp) plus the per-actor talk loop in d_npc.cpp.

_bmg.reader: JMessage::TParse / TResource (src/JSystem/JMessage/resource.cpp, include/JSystem/JMessage/data.h) with Wind Waker's own fopMsgM_msgGet_c on top (f_op_msg_mng.cpp:1547-1608)

header.0x10: u8 encoding (TParse_THeader::get_encoding; 1 on the USA disc)

_bmg.blocks: each block is { char[4] fourcc, u32 size-including-header } and is 32-byte aligned. zel_00.bmg has INF1 + DAT1 only; there is no MID1 and no STR1 on this disc (measured)

entry.struct: JMSMesgEntry_c (include/f_op/f_op_msg_mng.h:22-40); 0x18 bytes, matching the measured entry_size of 24

fields.name: mDataOffs
fields.meaning: byte offset into DAT1. 0 means 'no message' - getMessage() skips those entries entirely (f_op_msg_mng.cpp:1596-1597)
fields.measured: 85 of 4411 entries in zel_00.bmg have offset 0

fields.name: mMsgNo
fields.meaning: the id actors and events ask for. Lookup is a LINEAR SCAN over the entry table comparing mMsgNo, not an index (f_op_msg_mng.cpp:1588-1607) - so the id is unrelated to the entry's position and duplicates resolve to the first hit

fields.name: mItemPrice
fields.meaning: pushed to dComIfGp_setMessageRupee() when the box opens (f_op_msg_mng.cpp:467, d_msg.cpp:2325) - the shop price this message quotes

fields.name: mNextMsgNo
fields.meaning: the message to chain to. IN RETAIL THIS IS DEAD DATA: the only reader is guarded by fopMsgM_nextMsgFlagCheck(), and the static bool it returns is declared at f_op_msg_mng.cpp:55 and only ever assigned false (f_op_msg_mng.cpp:951) - there is no 'nextMsg = true' anywhere in the decomp. Chaining is done actor-side instead (see _flow). Separately, d_msg.cpp:2083-2091 reads mNextMsgNo == 1 or == 2 as 'which choice index counts as a cancel' and uses it only to pick the box-close sound
fields.measured: 113 entries non-zero; value 1 x2, value 2 x3, 108 real message ids (e.g. 401->601, 402->602, ...)

fields.name: field_0x0a
fields.meaning: UNKNOWN - the decomp names it field_0x0a and no code in src/ ever reads it

fields.name: mTextboxType
fields.meaning: selects the box screen and a pile of behaviour flags - see _box_styles

fields.name: mDrawType
fields.meaning: 0 = normal typing, A or B skips to the end of the page (d_msg.cpp:2687-2695); 1 = the page is drawn instantly unless a hard wait (field_0x296) is pending (d_msg.cpp:2696-2702); 2 = neither branch fires, so the page types out and cannot be skipped

fields.name: mTextboxPosition
fields.meaning: 0 = auto: project the player's eyePos, and if the result is above g_msgHIO.field_0x6e use 3 (top) else 1 (bottom); 1 = bottom (y = 480 - height - 0x13); 2 = screen centre (y = 240 - height/2); 3 = top (y = pane origin + 0x20)

fields.name: mItemImage
fields.meaning: icon shown in an item box; 255 = none
fields.measured: 255 in 4116 entries, 0 in 0 (the unused entries), 193 other distinct values

fields.name: mTextAlignment
fields.meaning: 1 = left, 2 = right, 0 or 3 = centre on centerLineWidth. BUT on USA stringShift() forces the value to 1 unless it is exactly 3 or the box type is 0xD - so in practice only alignment 3 (6 messages) and every box-type-0xD message are centred

fields.name: mInitialSound
fields.meaning: if non-zero, mDoAud_messageSePlay(mInitialSound, NULL, roomReverb) when the box opens - the speaker's voice grunt

fields.name: mInitialCamera
fields.meaning: dComIfGp_setMesgCameraAttrInfo(); values 1..5 additionally trip a branch in dMsg_Execute (d_msg.cpp:2326-2330)

fields.name: mInitialAnimation
fields.meaning: dComIfGp_setMesgAnimeAttrInfo() - the speaker's talking animation, read back by the NPC's anmAtr()

fields.name: field_0x16 (lines per box)
fields.meaning: how many lines fit before the box has to break to a new page: getString() compares its running lineCount against this after every newline
fields.note: gcrip/formats/bmg.py currently decodes a u16 'lines_per_box' at 0x15. That happens to give the right number only because field_0x15 is always 0 on this disc; the field is really the single byte at 0x16

DAT1.meaning: one NUL-terminated string per entry, at mDataOffs. Single-byte text on the USA disc; JMessage treats 0x81-0x9F/0xE0-0xFC as Shift-JIS lead bytes when the resource's encoding says so (TResourceContainer::IsLeadByte, TProcessor::process_character_)
DAT1.scanning: a NUL inside an escape sequence's payload is common (a bare {name} tag is 1A 05 00 00 00), so the string end must be found by skipping each escape by its size byte, exactly as the game does with 'count += bmgData[count + 1]'

files_on_the_USA_disc.res/Msg/bmgres.arc -> archive/zel_00.bmg: 4411 entries, group 0 - every message in the game
files_on_the_USA_disc.res/Msg/bmgresh.arc -> bmgresh/zel_01.bm: 15 entries, group 1 - the ancient-Hyrulean renderings. fopMsgM_hyrule_language_check() (f_op_msg_mng.cpp:275-302) swaps to this file for ids 0xD49,0xD4B,0xD4D,0xD4F,0xD51,0xD53,0xD54,0xD55,0xD57,0xD59,0x1178,0x117A,0x1389,0x138A,0x196E while dComIfGs_getClearCount() == 0. Measured: all 15 entries are box type 12, and their ids are exactly that set
files_on_the_USA_disc.note: the JPN/demo builds pick the file with sprintf("zel_%02d.bmg", msgNo >> 16); the USA build hard-codes zel_00/zel_01, so the high half of a u32 message number no longer selects a file. It still selects a PROCESS: msgNo >> 16 == 0x63 creates the telescope/scope process and == 0x59 the picto-box process (f_op_msg_mng.cpp:455-458)

color_bmc.layout: 'MGCLbmc1' header then one CLT1 block: u16 entryNum, u16 pad, then entryNum u32 RGBA colours (clt1_header, f_op_msg_mng.cpp:45-49)
color_bmc.note: gcrip/formats/bmg.py's COLORS table lists FFFFFF/FF5A5A/78FF78/7878FF/FFFF32/82FFFF/DC6EFF/A0A0A0/FF8200 - that is the dMesg colorTable in d_mesg.cpp:679-690, which belongs to the OTHER message renderer (dMesg_tSequenceProcessor, used for the hint-stone/JMessage path), not to the main text box. The main box uses color.bmc

escape.tag_word: the three bytes after size are packed into a u32 tag; JMessage::data::getTagGroup(tag) = (tag >> 16) & 0xFF, getTagCode(tag) = tag & 0xFFFF

newline.meaning: a real line break; getString() bumps lineCount and compares it with the entry's field_0x16

group_0.meaning: Wind Waker's own control codes (enum MsgControlCodes, f_op_msg_mng.cpp:144-222). Dispatched by a long else-if chain in fopMsgM_msgDataProc_c::getString that tests bmgData[count+2]==0 && bmgData[count+3]==0 && bmgData[count+4]==code - i.e. only the low byte of the code is ever matched

codes.name: WAIT_INPUT

codes.name: DUMMY

codes.name: WAIT
codes.meaning: waitTimer = arg frames: typing pauses that long, then continues in the same box. Skipped when field_0x299 (shortCut) is set; sets field_0x296 for box types 0/1/5/8/C/E

group_1.meaning: play a sound effect: mDoAud_messageSePlay(code, actorPosition, roomReverb). Code 8 is the one special case - it is played with a NULL position (2D)
group_1.source: src/f_op/f_op_msg_mng.cpp:5389-5406; also src/d/d_mesg.cpp:610-620 for the dMesg renderer
group_1.id_space: unresolved - JAIZelBasic::messageSePlay is /* Nonmatching */ in the decomp (src/JAZelAudio/JAIZelBasic.cpp:824-827), so nothing maps a message SE index to a sound bank entry

group_2.meaning: camera cue: dComIfGp_setMesgCameraTagInfo(code). d_msg.cpp:2684 latches it into sub_msg_class::mMesgCameraTagInfo when the box repositions

group_3.meaning: speaker animation cue: dComIfGp_setMesgAnimeTagInfo(code); the NPC reads it back in its anmAtr()

codes.name: SpclCode_COLOR
codes.meaning: sets the text colour to palette entry arg[0]. Which palette depends on the box: the default is fopMsgM_getColorTable(n) = entry n of CLT1 in res/Msg/bmgres.arc:color.bmc; box types 2/6/7 (wooden signs), box type 0xB and messages 0x42-0x4B each use their own hard-coded 9-entry table in f_op_msg_mng.cpp

codes.name: SpclCode_UNK1 (font size)
codes.meaning: font size as a percentage: field_0x148 = fontSize * (arg / 100.0) + 0.5. A value over 100 costs an extra text line (field_0x29D)

codes.name: SpclCode_RUBY
codes.meaning: furigana: arg[0] = how many base characters the reading covers, then the reading itself as Shift-JIS pairs. The body is compiled out for PAL and never appears in the USA BMG (0 occurrences measured)

reserved_groups_never_used_here.0xFF: JMessage system tag - TProcessor::do_tag_ forwards it to do_systemTagCode(); Wind Waker's override handles colour/size/ruby (src/JSystem/JMessage/processor.cpp:161-177)
reserved_groups_never_used_here.0xFE: JMessage 'word' substitution - pushCurrent(mControl->on_word(code)) (src/JSystem/JMessage/processor.cpp:169). Unused by Wind Waker's own reader; 0 occurrences
reserved_groups_never_used_here.0xF6: JMessage select-begin, u16 offset table (process_select_limited_). 0 occurrences - Wind Waker does choices with group 0 codes 0x08/0x09/0x1E/0x1F instead
reserved_groups_never_used_here.0xF5: JMessage select-begin, u32 offset table (process_select_). 0 occurrences

_frequency.measured_over: res/Msg/bmgres.arc -> archive/zel_00.bmg from the USA disc (4411 INF1 entries, 85 of them empty, 533400 bytes of DAT1)
_frequency.method: every DAT1 string reached from a non-zero mDataOffs was walked byte by byte; each 0x1A was decoded as group/code and counted. 'count' is total occurrences, 'messages' is how many distinct messages contain at least one

zel_01_bmg.note: the 15 Hyrulean strings contain no control codes at all

what_a_remake_actually_has_to_handle: 0xFF:0x0000 colour - 5232 uses in 1751 messages, by far the most common tag
0x00:0x0007 wait - 1209 uses in 731 messages; 10, 20, 30 and 15 frames are 90% of them
0x00:0x0001 / 0x00:0x0002 instant-draw on/off - 622 uses in 272 messages (they pair up)
0x00:0x0008 two-option choice - 214 messages; 0x00:0x0009 three-option - 9 messages; 0x00:0x001E/0x001F horizontal choice - 14 messages
0xFF:0x0001 font size - 144 uses in 103 messages, only 7 distinct percentages
everything else (the 40-odd value registers) is 1-11 uses each: ~180 tags across the whole game, essentially all in minigame and shop text

_flow.who_drives_it: there is no d_msg_flow.cpp in Wind Waker. The page pump is fopMsgM_msgDataProc_c::getString/stringSet (f_op_msg_mng.cpp), the box process is dMsg_Execute (d_msg.cpp:2620-3020), and the conversation is driven by the actor's own talk loop

status_enum.source: include/f_op/f_op_msg.h:9-34 (fopMsg_MessageStatus_e); the live value lives in msg_class::mStatus at 0xF8 and is copied out of fopMsgM_msgDataProc_c::mesgStatus each frame (d_msg.cpp:2710)

values.0x08: SELECT_2 - a two-option choice is on screen
values.0x09: SELECT_3 - a three-option choice is on screen
values.0x0A: CLOSE_WAIT - waiting for input before closing
values.0x0E: MSG_DISPLAYED - the page is finished and the actor may act
values.0x0F: MSG_CONTINUES - the actor asked for another message
values.0x10: MSG_ENDS - the actor is done talking
values.0x15: INPUT - number entry (auction) or Wind Waker practice

_flow.page_end: when getString reaches the string's NUL it plays the page-advance sound mDoAud_messageSePlay(0, NULL, reverb) - suppressed for box types 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 0xB and 0xD - and then sets mesgStatus to CLOSE_WAIT if an auto/hand send flag is pending, otherwise MSG_DISPLAYED (src/f_op/f_op_msg_mng.cpp:3695-3724 and src/f_op/f_op_msg_mng.cpp:5744-5776)

chaining.how_it_really_works: the actor polls its msg_class every frame. When it sees mStatus == MSG_DISPLAYED it calls its own virtual next_msgStatus(&msgNo); if that returns MSG_CONTINUES it writes the next id into msgNo and calls fopMsgM_messageSet(msgNo), which reuses the open box. Returning MSG_ENDS (the base-class default) lets the box close
chaining.source: src/d/d_npc.cpp:663-696 (fopNpc_npc_c::talk), include/d/d_npc.h:272 (virtual u16 next_msgStatus(u32*) { return fopMsgStts_MSG_ENDS_e; }), src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:443+ for a real override (a switch on the current id)
chaining.bmg_side: mNextMsgNo (INF1 0x08) would do the same automatically, but its guard flag is never set true in retail - see _bmg.entry.mNextMsgNo

choices.authoring: a choice is not a separate structure. The message text contains 0x1A 05 00 00 08 (or 09), and the option strings are simply the lines that follow, one per line. 0x1E/0x1F mark a horizontal (left/right) pair instead
choices.runtime: getString sets selectFlag (Select_ON / Select_YOKO / Select_AUCTION), resets lineCount and moves the four output buffers to selectMessage[0..3], then sets mesgStatus to SELECT_2 / SELECT_3 / SELECT_YOKO. dMsg_Execute then runs selectCheck2/selectCheck3/selectCheckYoko every frame, which reads the stick and writes the highlighted row into msg_class::mSelectNum (0-based) and moves the cursor pane
choices.commit: when the player presses A (or B with dActStts_CANCEL_e), d_msg.cpp:2064-2100 hides the choice panes, plays the close sound (cancel-flavoured if the pick is the last row, or if mNextMsgNo is 1 and the pick is row 0, or if mNextMsgNo is 2) and sets mStatus = MSG_DISPLAYED
choices.how_the_actor_learns_the_pick: it reads msg_class::mSelectNum (include/f_op/f_op_msg.h:47, 'The index of the choice the player selected'). Typical actor code is 'switch (mpCurrMsg->mSelectNum)' inside next_msgStatus - see src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bm1.cpp:1428 and 1457, d_a_npc_ba1.cpp:691, d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp:400-500
choices.cancel_button: dComIfGp_setMesgCancelButton(1) is set when the choice was dismissed with B; actors test dComIfGp_checkMesgCancelButton() (e.g. src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:516)

actor_side_api.open: fopMsgM_messageSet(u32 msgNo, fopAc_ac_c* actor) -> fpc_ProcID (f_op_msg_mng.cpp:512+). msgNo >> 16 == 0x63 opens the telescope process and == 0x59 the picto-box process; otherwise the entry's mTextboxType picks MSG2 (types 2/6/7) or MSG
actor_side_api.poll: fopMsgM_SearchByID(procId) -> msg_class*, then read mStatus / mSelectNum
actor_side_api.close: on BOX_CLOSED the actor writes MSG_DESTROYED into mStatus and forgets the proc id

_box_styles.screen_selection: dMsg_screenDataSet (d_msg.cpp:649-687) switches on mTextboxType: 5 -> hukidashi_05.blo, 1 and 9 -> hukidashi_09.blo, 0xE -> hukidashi_14.blo, everything else -> hukidashi_00.blo. Types 2/6/7 never reach it because fopMsgM_messageTypeSelect sends them to a different process entirely

types.name: talk
types.note: the ordinary speech bubble (hukidashi_00.blo). Draws a tail toward the speaker (dDlst_2DMSG_c::draw checks type 0 or 10)

types.name: item_get_special
types.note: uses the item screen hukidashi_09.blo; shows the item icon panes

types.name: sign
types.note: handled by a different process (fpcNm_MSG2_e -> d_message.cpp) with texture hukidashi_02.bti; no close sound; uses the sign colour table

types.name: demo
types.note: cutscene subtitle screen hukidashi_05.blo, 3 lines, no arrow pane, stringShift() force-sets field_0x299 so the whole page draws at once

types.name: sign_6
types.note: MSG2 process with texture hukidashi_06.bti (a second board style)

types.name: sign_7
types.note: MSG2 process with texture hukidashi_07.bti (a third board style)

types.name: type_8
types.note: no dedicated screen (falls to hukidashi_00.blo); only appears in the 0x04/0x07 wait list of 'boxes that honour a hard pause'

types.name: item_get
types.note: item screen hukidashi_09.blo; dItem_data::getTexture(msgNo - 101) supplies the icon, so message 101 + itemNo is the item-get text

types.name: talk_no_reposition
types.note: same screen as type 0 and also draws the speaker tail, but dMsg_Execute skips the 'follow the actor' reposition for it

types.name: type_B
types.note: own hard-coded colour table; 102 of its 181 entries are one line long

types.name: hyrulean
types.note: the ancient-Hyrulean rendering: fopMsgM_hyrule_language_check() redirects 15 specific ids to zel_01.bmg while clearCount == 0; also the only type whose player-name insertion is byte-wise on PAL

types.name: centered
types.note: the one box type that keeps mTextAlignment as authored instead of forcing left

types.name: wind_waker
types.note: the Wind Waker conducting screen hukidashi_14.blo (+ hukidashi_14_*.blo parts); no arrow pane; drives fopMsgStts_INPUT_e / DEMO_e / TACT_e

typing_speed.per_frame_budget: stringSet() takes a local budget r30 = g_msgHIO.field_0x6c at the top and, after each emitted character, does 'if (field_0x299 == 0 && field_0x29A == 0 && autoSendFlag == 0 && handSendFlag == 0 && selectFlag == Select_OFF) { if (r30 == 0) return; r30--; }'. dMeter_msg_HIO_c's constructor sets field_0x6c = 0, so the shipped speed is exactly ONE CHARACTER PER FRAME (60/s at NTSC). field_0x299 (the shortcut set by draw_type 1 or by pressing A/B on a draw_type 0 box), field_0x29A (control code 0x01) and a pending choice/auto/hand send all bypass the budget and finish the page in one frame
typing_speed.source: src/f_op/f_op_msg_mng.cpp:3663-3669 (r30 = g_msgHIO.field_0x6c), src/f_op/f_op_msg_mng.cpp:5713-5724 (the budget test), src/d/d_meter.cpp:370-440 (dMeter_msg_HIO_c::dMeter_msg_HIO_c, field_0x6c = 0)
typing_speed.sendSpeed_is_dead: fopMsgM_msgDataProc_c::sendSpeed is initialised to 1 and re-set to g_msgHIO.field_0x82 (= 2) on every box open (d_msg.cpp:785, 860, 922, 956, 2301), but nothing in f_op_msg_mng.cpp ever reads it. It is not the typing speed
typing_speed.extra_pause_on_punctuation: after a space (0x20, only when spaceFlag is set) or the Japanese 0x8140 / 0x8141 / 0x878C, waitTimer is set to spaceTimer, which d_msg.cpp sets to 2 on every box open (d_msg.cpp:786, 861, 923) - so the typing hesitates 2 frames at every space

other_shipped_tuning_values.lineWidth set by d_msg.cpp: 0x1F7 = 503 px normally, 0x1A3 = 419 px for item boxes

per_character_sound.finding: Wind Waker does NOT play a sound per typed character. The sounds around a text box are: mDoAud_talkIn() when the box opens (d_msg.cpp:2657); mDoAud_messageSePlay(mInitialSound, ...) once at open if the entry has one; mDoAud_messageSePlay(0, NULL, reverb) once at the end of each page (suppressed for box types 2/5/6/7/9/0xB/0xD); mDoAud_talkOut() plus JA_SE_TALK_WIN_CLOSE or JA_SE_TALK_SEL_CANCEL when it closes (dMsg_setCloseSound, d_msg.cpp:1796-1805); and whatever a group-1 escape asks for mid-string

_box_styles.close_sound: dMsg_setCloseSound(msg, cancelFlag): JA_SE_TALK_SEL_CANCEL when cancelFlag is set or dComIfGp_getDoStatusForce() == dActStts_CANCEL_e, otherwise JA_SE_TALK_WIN_CLOSE (d_msg.cpp:1796-1805)

what_gcrip_already_does.gcrip/formats/bmg.py: parses the header, INF1 and DAT1 correctly, walks escapes by their size byte, and renders them as readable {tags}. Its group-0 name table matches the decomp's enum names one-for-one for the codes the decomp actually names, and the value-tag names it borrows from the randomizer are confirmed by this pass for 0x20, 0x22, 0x23, 0x26, 0x28, 0x29, 0x2B, 0x2F, 0x32-0x35, 0x37, 0x38, 0x3B, 0x45-0x4A
what_gcrip_already_does.gcrip/msg.py: dumps every message to out/rip/GZLE01/text/messages.json (id, index, text, attrs, raw_hex) and a Markdown mirror
what_gcrip_already_does.gcrip/godot.py: copies that json to res://messages.json, builds a flat {id: text} dictionary (line 3237-3242) and shows it with Game.show_message / show_messages / _paginate; the {tags} are left in the string verbatim

corrections_this_pass_found_in_bmg.py: lines_per_box is decoded as a u16 at 0x15; JMSMesgEntry_c says 0x15, 0x16 and 0x17 are three separate u8 and only 0x16 is ever read (as the per-box line limit). The number comes out right today only because field_0x15 is 0 in every entry on this disc

the COLORS table is dMesg's palette (d_mesg.cpp:679-690), not the text box's. The box reads color.bmc: index 1 is FF6400 (orange-red) not FF5A5A, 2 is 00FF00, 3 is 7878FF, 4 is FFFF3C, 5 is 00FFFF, 6 is FF00FF, 7 is 828282, 8 is FF8000 - and box types 2/6/7, box type 0xB and messages 0x42-0x4B override it entirely

TEXT_BOX_TYPES is missing 6, 7, 8, 0xB and mislabels 0xA: types 6 and 7 are two more sign boards handled by a separate process, 0xB has its own palette, and 0xA is an ordinary talk box that simply does not follow the actor
text_alignment values are 0/1/3 in the data (not 3/4), and USA forces everything except exactly 3 (or box type 0xD) to left

draw_type names 'instant'/'slow' are backwards for what the code does: 0 means normal typing that A or B can skip, 1 means the page appears at once unless a hard wait is pending, 2 means it types out and cannot be skipped
next_message_id is dead in retail (its guard flag is never set true); the values 1 and 2 in that field are a cancel-index marker for the close sound, not message ids
minimum_useful_remake_order: 1. Reveal timing: type one character per frame; on 0x00:0x0001 dump the rest of the page instantly and on 0x00:0x0002 go back to per-character. That plus 0x00:0x0007 (wait N frames) covers 1841 of the 2100-odd non-colour tags in the game
2. Colour: 0xFF:0x0000 with the color.bmc palette. 5232 uses; index 0 (white) and index 1 (FF6400) are 99% of them, so a two-colour implementation already reads right
3. Player name: 0x00:0x0000 -> the save's name. 332 messages break without it
4. Page breaks: honour field_0x16 (usually 4, 3 for cutscene subtitles, 1 for the 102 one-line type-0xB boxes) instead of a fixed paginator
5. Choices: on 0x00:0x0008 / 0x00:0x0009 treat the following lines as options, expose a select index, and hand it back to the NPC the way mSelectNum does. 223 messages
6. Icons: 0x0A-0x1D plus 0x27/0x2A/0x39/0x3A map to the acticon/button glyphs already ripped under out/rip/GZLE01/res/Msg/acticon.arc

7. Box shape: mTextboxType picks the frame (talk / item / demo subtitle / sign / Wind Waker), mTextboxPosition picks top / bottom / centre / auto, mInitialSound is the speaker's grunt, mInitialAnimation is the talking clip
8. Value registers last - 40 codes, ~180 uses, all in shops and minigames. Rendering them as 0 is survivable
not_determined: the shipped value of g_msgHIO.field_0x82 (characters revealed per frame) and the rest of the g_msgHIO / g_msgDHIO tuning block - the decomp exposes the struct but not its initialiser
what any group-1 sound code actually plays: JAIZelBasic::messageSePlay is Nonmatching in the decomp, so the message-SE index space is not mapped to the sound bank
the meaning of INF1 field_0x0a (values 0x00/0x54/0x60/0x71/0x78/0x85/0x8E on this disc) - no code in src/ reads it
INF1 field_0x14, field_0x15 and field_0x17 - never read, and 0 in every entry anyway

which of the five codes sharing the tag_rupee handler (0x21/0x24/0x25/0x2C/0x36) means what: the USA code path is identical for all five and only reads dComIfGp_getMessageCountNumber(); the distinct names in bmg.py and in the decomp's own comments are guesses

the bodies of the USA tag_stock_* and tag_input_* helpers (they are declared in include/f_op/f_op_msg_mng.h under '#if VERSION >= VERSION_USA' but the decomp routes to them without showing what they read)
the group-2 camera and group-3 animation code spaces - the escapes only forward a number to dComIfGp_setMesgCameraTagInfo / setMesgAnimeTagInfo, and the consumer is per-actor
